summary: El Dorado County enclosed tower built 1936 with CCC labor; no longer used for fire detection, now a repeater site inside the Pine Hill Preserve; listed as standing.

facts.design: BC-301 cab atop an L-701 tower; major tower revisions in 1972

staffing.status: operated by CalFire; may be staffed as needed

facts.agency: California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection

events.note: CCC crews building a road to the summit and a lookout station
Built 1936; Register says constructed by the CCC
Summer lookout man La Verne Campbell reported at Pine Hill
Oswald family stationed at the lookout for the summer
Forest Lookouts timeline says the lookout was remodeled
Register says there were major tower revisions
CDF announced intention to dispose of the site as surplus
Property transferred to the California Department of Fish and Wildlife; with county and BLM land, the Pine Hill Preserve was established
Registered July 30, 2018 as US 1283, CA 125; nominated by Michael Guerin

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Forest Lookouts timeline gives a 1971 remodel; the Register gives major tower revisions in 1972. Both are kept as separate events because the sources do not say whether they describe the same work.
The Register gives 2,059 ft (628 m); Peakbagging gives 2062 ft. The record's 627.6 m matches the Register.

notes_for_editor: No access key is set: the BLM open-access statement covers BLM parcels in the Preserve, and no source read describes the lookout compound or says whether the public may climb or enter it. The lookout shares the summit with repeater towers, which may restrict entry. No notable fire is recorded in the sources read. Staffing evidence is a December 2004 photo caption and 1937-38 newspaper items. One WebSearch was run for this tower; the Wikipedia reserve article and CNPS tour pages were seen in results but not fetched.
